thesis: Confirmed Q2 FY2026 results showed net sales up 5.2%, same-store sales up 3.5%, customer traffic up 2.0%, and GAAP operating profit up 29.2%, alongside raised FY2026 sales and comparable-sales guidance. The strongest negative is that tariff refunds contributed about 81 basis points to gross margin and 66 basis points to operating margin; however, management said results exceeded expectations before the refund benefit and its raised outlook assumes no material second-half refund benefit, so the core traffic and comparable-sales improvement still supports a long read.
invalidation: Comparable-sales or traffic growth turns negative, or management cuts the raised FY2026 sales/comparable-sales guidance after results excluding tariff-refund benefits fail to sustain the operating improvement.
sources: Dollar General Q2 FY2026 earnings release: https://investor.dollargeneral.com/news-detail/dollar-general-corporation-reports-second-quarter-2026-results/71b3816e-10a9-4028-845a-d161637e745b
Dollar General Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q mirror: https://financialfilings.com/filings/dollar-general-corporation/interim-quarterly-report/2026/57717498/

thesis: Confirmed Q4 FY2026 results showed GMV up 36% and revenue up 33%, with FY2027 guidance for GMV above $64 billion and GAAP operating margin above 14.5%. The strongest negative is that quarterly credit-loss provision rose about 42%, faster than GMV; however, full-year provision declined to 1.6% of GMV from 1.7% while revenue less transaction costs improved to 4.2% of GMV from 4.0%, so current credit-cost evidence does not overturn the positive operating read.
invalidation: Credit-loss provision as a share of GMV rises above the prior-year rate while revenue less transaction costs as a share of GMV deteriorates, or management cuts the FY2027 GMV or GAAP operating-margin guidance.

thesis: Confirmed Q4 FY2026 revenue and ARR each rose 16%, and management issued FY2027 revenue and free-cash-flow guidance that supports continued demand. The strongest positive does not change the avoid read because Nutanix also disclosed a 5% workforce reduction, hardware-supply and renewal-cohort constraints, and an active DOJ procurement inquiry involving historical conduct by a former employee who pleaded guilty to procurement-related conspiracy and wire-fraud charges; the completed operations-linked governance failure and unresolved probe outweigh the reported momentum.
invalidation: The DOJ matter closes without adverse company findings while restructuring completes without weakening growth, and subsequent results sustain ARR growth and the FY2027 revenue/free-cash-flow guidance.
sources: U.S. Department of Justice, U.S. v. Scott Reefe: https://www.justice.gov/atr/case/us-v-scott-reefe

thesis: Confirmed Q2 FY2027 results showed revenue up 21% and ARR up 22%, with raised FY2027 revenue and non-GAAP operating-income guidance. The strongest negative is weaker per-share economics from a higher diluted-share count and GAAP gross margin declining to 72% from 75%; however, non-GAAP operating margin improved to 10% from 2% on the same basis and the operating-income outlook rose, so current operating leverage and recurring-revenue growth still support a long read.
invalidation: ARR or revenue growth materially decelerates while GAAP gross margin continues to contract, or management cuts the raised FY2027 revenue or non-GAAP operating-income guidance.

thesis: Confirmed Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 12.5% and management raised its FY2026 outlook, but the operating evidence is mixed: Personal Systems revenue rose 18% while units fell 16% and segment operating margin was only 4.6%, while Printing revenue and supplies revenue declined. Those demand and margin counterpoints outweigh the guide-up, and a derivative-settlement final approval hearing is scheduled for September 18, 2026, so the net read is avoid.
invalidation: Personal Systems unit growth recovers while segment margin expands, Printing and supplies revenue stabilize, and the September 18 derivative-settlement hearing resolves without material adverse company impact.
sources: U.S. District Court derivative-settlement preliminary approval order: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCOURTS-cand-4_21-cv-04805/pdf/USCOURTS-cand-4_21-cv-04805-0.pdf
